properties.self-inverse: applying the same value twice undoes it: a ^ x ^ x = a
properties.invertible: every step has a known undo: a + x - x = a
properties.commutative: operand order does not matter: a + b = b + a
properties.associative: grouping does not matter, so a running fold works: (a + b) + c = a + (b + c)
properties.identity element: a neutral value e with a op e = a: 0 for + ^ gcd, -Infinity for max, +Infinity for min
properties.idempotent: combining a value with itself changes nothing: max(a, a) = a
properties.selective: the result is always one of the operands: max(a, b) is a or b
properties.divides its inputs: the result divides every operand, so folding more values can only shrink it
properties.works per bit: each bit position is computed independently of the others
properties.carries between bits: bit positions interact: a carry moves into the next position
properties.cancels any k-fold repeat: a value that occurs exactly k times leaves no trace, for any chosen k
properties.isolates one bit: keeps a single set bit and clears the rest: x & -x keeps the lowest one
properties.O(1) extra space: a fixed number of variables besides the input, however large the input
properties.single pass: reads the input once, front to back
properties.O(1) lookup: asks 'seen x?' or 'what is stored for x?' in (expected) constant time
properties.stores a value per key: remembers something per key (a count, an index), not only that it was seen
properties.presence only: remembers whether a key was seen and nothing else
properties.arbitrary keys: keys can be any value: strings, huge or negative numbers
properties.bounded key range: keys come from a small known range (26 letters, 0..n), so an array indexed by key works
properties.two moving indexes: two indexes that each move in one direction only, so the scan is O(n)
properties.from both ends: the two indexes start at opposite ends and move toward each other
properties.window moves right: both indexes move left to right; the range between them is the current window
properties.monotone condition: only correct when validity changes once as a range grows (no negatives in a sum)
properties.needs sorted input: only correct once the input is sorted
properties.O(n log n) time: costs about n log n comparisons, more than one linear pass
properties.makes equal values adjacent: afterwards equal (and close) values sit next to each other
properties.O(log n) per query: each question halves the remaining range, so it costs about log n steps
properties.range query in O(1): after O(n) setup, any contiguous range's total is one subtraction
properties.needs an inverse: only works over an operation that can be undone (+ with -, ^ with ^); max has none
properties.keeps every prefix: stores all n prefix values, so any (l, r) range can be asked later
properties.handles negatives: stays correct when values can be negative (a sliding window does not)
properties.needs a majority: only correct when one value occurs more than n/2 times
properties.last-in-first-out: the most recently added element is the first one taken out
properties.next-greater lookup: for every element, finds the nearest later element that is larger (flip for smaller)
properties.amortized O(n): each element is added and removed at most once, so the total work is linear
properties.overlaps become adjacent: after sorting by start, every interval that overlaps the current group comes right after it
properties.earliest end first: choosing the interval that ends first leaves the most room for the rest
properties.greedy: commits to the locally best choice and never revisits it
properties.O(log n) push and pop-min: insert and remove-the-smallest each cost about log n; flip the comparison for largest
properties.partial order: only the top element is guaranteed to be in place; the rest is not sorted
